definitions.note: to box is to spar, to fight with fists

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: spare means free or unoccupied, as in spare time

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a box is free of charge, answered with a hesitant 'not quite'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of SPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparring is boxing practice, so the verb to box can mean to spar.

clue.text: Last character to be driven out of Cornish town as punishment

indicators.note: driven out of means expelled, so the letter is removed from the town name

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the far south-west county of England
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A final resident is banished from a Cornish town as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-imposed suffering to atone for wrongdoing, a form of punishment.

clue.text: Heath brought up on foremost of yachts, very spacious

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a moor is open heathland

indicators.note: foremost of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A yachtsman named Heath brought aboard, finding the yacht very spacious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' could be a person, but it is the landscape; 'brought up' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means having plenty of space, the same as spacious.

indicators.note: a cracked vase is broken up, so its letters with those of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hides a broken vase and helpfully leaves some glue to mend it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue is a substance that sticks things together, a classic example of the general term.

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the apex is the top point

explanation.surface: An impressionist's short-sleeved top.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy their manner, which is what a mimic does.

clue.text: Taken by surprise as bowler was?

definitions.meaning: badly shaken or stunned, as if dealt a heavy blow
in cricket a batsman striking the ball over the boundary on the full scores six runs off the bowler

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a bowler whose delivery is struck over the boundary without bouncing has been punished for six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stunned and shocked is the idiom, and literally a bowler whose ball was clouted for a maximum suffered it.

indicators.note: in ruin means wrecked, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A class of students examining the remains of a ruined site.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class of students meeting to discuss a subject.

clue.text: Put a price on uranium discovered in glen

indicators.note: discovered in means found inside, so the symbol sits within the valley word

parts.note: a vale is a valley, like a glen
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Valuing a uranium find made in a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To value goods is to estimate their worth, which is to put a price on them.

indicators.note: aboard means on board, carried inside, so one piece sits within the other
involved here means tangled or complicated, so the admiral's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An offensive involving Admiral Nelson on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is rude and disrespectful, which is offensive; the two adjectives are synonyms.

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A man is taken ill at his workplace, a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill is a works or plant where goods are made, as in a cotton or steel works.

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for zero is taken away

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic messenger
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Resenting a diplomat who is lacking in anything at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone their good fortune is to resent it, which is the verb sense of covet or resent.

indicators.note: full of means containing, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a ship that founders sinks
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A sink overflowing with big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish such as plaice or a fluke is named this way, so it is a type of fish.

indicators.note: after means the first-named piece comes second, following the other

parts.note: flat is the British word for an apartment
broke means snapped, broken in two

explanation.surface: Something snapped once a flat had been cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaned out' looks like housework, but it means penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaned out is an idiom for having lost all one's money, completely penniless.

clue.text: One employed to entertain man in charge is hand-picked

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: An entertainer has been specially chosen by the man in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man in charge' reads as a boss, but 'man' belongs to the definition and the letters are tucked into 'charge is hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained to entertain male guests with conversation, music and dance.

clue.text: Hide and seek? Not half, on Greek island

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word, here its first two letters

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Playing hide and seek on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', but here it halves 'seek' to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, a verb sense matching hide.

parts.note: rife means widespread, common everywhere

explanation.surface: Unrest has broken out across the street and become general.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or bitter disagreement, a close synonym of discord.

clue.text: Wild about editor describing US government?

indicators.note: about means around, so the wild word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: feral means wild, untamed

explanation.surface: An unhinged rant about an editor, with a hint of political commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describing the national government of the United States, as distinct from the states.

parts.note: jet as a colour is deep black
to box is to pack into a container

explanation.surface: A recorder stowed inside a jet aircraft's pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' suggests an aircraft, fitting the flight recorder, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's flight recorder is popularly called by this name, though it is usually orange.

clue.text: Sign made by one supporter following Liverpool's first

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the pieces come after the initial letter
first means the initial letter of the city name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A sign held up by a football supporter behind Liverpool's leading player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a football fan, but it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

indicators.note: heading means going in front of, so the first piece leads the compass letter

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: Travelling at no cost while heading eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading East' looks like a direction of travel, but it places RID before E.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to be carried along in a vehicle or on horseback, a way to journey.

clue.text: Shock that head is leaving? I'll say!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which leaves, so it is removed

parts.note: a fright is a sudden shock

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that the head teacher is departing, and emphatically agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation of agreement, 'Right!' is equivalent to 'Absolutely!' or 'I'll say!'

clue.text: Orchestra's leader invested in gong? Blow me!

indicators.note: invested in means placed within, as an honour is conferred inside a ceremony

parts.note: gong is slang for a medal or honour, here the OBE, Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader is given an honour, and someone exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow me!' reads as an exclamation of surprise but is a cryptic definition of an instrument you blow; 'gong' is British slang for an honour like the OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument played by blowing, so it might cheekily say 'blow me'.

clue.text: Source of fruit provided by old park keeper, Yosemite, primarily

parts.note: a ranger looks after a national park

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the initial letter is used

explanation.surface: A Yosemite ranger from long ago is credited with a fruit supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A glasshouse for growing citrus trees yields oranges, so it is a source of fruit.

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A remark that a short piece of writing amounts to just a couple of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite and all can both mean completely, as in 'all alone' and 'quite alone'.

parts.note: fare is food, as in simple fare
a well is a source of water or oil

explanation.surface: A food supply described as long-lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal goodbye, and this word is a formal parting greeting.

indicators.note: read aloud means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: The ending of a story being read out to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative or yarn, a synonym of story.
